position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: flamenco rumba × bachata × hip-hop / pop (post-Rosalía mainstream)
position_in_era.historical_role: The most commercially dominant post-Rosalía flamenco translation. *El Madrileño* (2021) was the best-selling album in Spain that year, debuted #1 on Spanish charts, #8 US Latin Albums; explicitly a tribute to Spanish roots music with twelve of fourteen tracks built around collaborations with flamenco / Latin folk / rock figures. 'Tú Me Dejaste De Querer' (with Niño de Elche and La Húngara) is the rumba-bachata hinge piece.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Released 26 February 2021 on Sony Music. Co-produced by Tangana and Alizzz. Tangana described 'Tú Me Dejaste De Querer' as 'the most important song of his career'.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Tangana (Antón Álvarez Alfaro) shifted from hip-hop to root-music collaboration; Niño de Elche (avant-flamenco) and La Húngara (rumba/copla) embody the translation aesthetic on the lead single.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Madrid; the album's title and frame insist on Madrid as a meeting-point for Spanish-language root traditions across the Atlantic.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Flamenco guitar, palmas, cajón blended with bachata-style guitar phrasing and electronic beat production.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Best-selling album in Spain 2021; broke the post-Rosalía flamenco-pop export market into US Latin charts.
